MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How many factors does 36 have? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 11
   C. 9
   D. 8

2. How many factors does 45 have? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 7
   C. 6
   D. 5

3. Round 379 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 370
   B. 300
   C. 380
   D. 390

4. Round 831 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 800
   B. 820
   C. 830
   D. 840

5. A school has 1,845 pupils in the lower classes and 2,367 pupils in the upper classes. How many pupils are in the school? (1 mark)
   A. 4,312 pupils
   B. 4,202 pupils
   C. 3,102 pupils
   D. 4,212 pupils

6. Which word in a problem tells you to subtract? (1 mark)
   A. Difference
   B. Total
   C. Sum
   D. Altogether

7. Work out 36 × 24. (1 mark)
   A. 874
   B. 216
   C. 854
   D. 864

8. What is the next number in the pattern 3, 6, 12, 24, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 48
   B. 36
   C. 30
   D. 27

9. What is 52 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 1,560
   B. 15,600
   C. 82
   D. 156

10. What is 700 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 70
   B. 8
   C. 700
   D. 7

11. What is 92 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 22
   B. 33
   C. 24
   D. 23

12. What is 91 ÷ 7? (1 mark)
   A. 23
   B. 14
   C. 13
   D. 12

13. Change 17/5 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 4 2/5
   B. 2 3/5
   C. 3 3/5
   D. 3 2/5

14. Which is greater, 1.2 or 1.19? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot be told
   B. 1.19
   C. 1.2
   D. They are equal

15. Which expression shows "6 less than k"? (1 mark)
   A. 6k
   B. k − 6
   C. 6 − k
   D. k + 6

16. What does 4m mean? (1 mark)
   A. 4 + m
   B. 4 × m
   C. 4 ÷ m
   D. 4 − m

17. A pencil starts at the 3 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 11 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 14 cm
   B. 11 cm
   C. 9 cm
   D. 8 cm

18. Change 400 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 40 cm
   B. 5 m
   C. 4 m
   D. 4 m 50 cm

19. A square is covered with 10 rows of 10 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 40 square units
   B. 20 square units
   C. 100 square units
   D. 110 square units

20. A square is covered with 5 rows of 5 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 20 square units
   B. 30 square units
   C. 10 square units
   D. 25 square units

21. A cuboid has a volume of 100 blocks. One layer has 20 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 120
   B. 5
   C. 6
   D. 80

22. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 28 blocks
   B. 35 blocks
   C. 10 blocks
   D. 30 blocks

23. A cuboid is 4 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 4 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 68 blocks
   B. 64 blocks
   C. 12 blocks
   D. 16 blocks

24. What is 2 L + 1 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/4 L
   B. 3 1/2 L
   C. 3 3/4 L
   D. 4 L

25. How many 1/4 kg masses balance a 1 kg mass? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 4
   C. 8
   D. 2

26. How many minutes does the minute hand take to go once round the clock face? (1 mark)
   A. 12 minutes
   B. 60 minutes
   C. 30 minutes
   D. 24 minutes

27. Change 35 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 5 weeks
   B. 6 weeks
   C. 5 weeks 1 days
   D. 0 weeks 5 days

28. Which formula gives the change from a purchase? (1 mark)
   A. Total cost × amount paid
   B. Amount paid + total cost
   C. Total cost − amount paid
   D. Amount paid − total cost

29. What is a plane figure? (1 mark)
   A. A solid object
   B. A flat shape
   C. A kind of aeroplane
   D. A curved line only

30. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 10
   C. 11
   D. 12

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Find the volume of a cube with sides of 4 blocks. (3 marks)

32. Write these times using a.m. or p.m.: (a) waking up at half past six in the morning, (b) school ending at a quarter past three in the afternoon, (c) supper at half past seven at night. (3 marks)

33. Tabitha has 2,450 eggs. She gets 3,875 more. How many eggs does she have now? (3 marks)

34. Sort these fractions into proper, improper and mixed: 3/8, 11/5, 2 1/2, 9/9, 7/10. (4 marks)

35. Wairimu had d shillings and spent 45 shillings. Write an expression for what she has left and find it when d = 100. (3 marks)

36. A classroom floor is covered with 15 rows of 10 tiles. How many tiles are used? If 6 tiles are broken and must be replaced, how many tiles are unbroken? (4 marks)

37. Explain how you can compare the areas of two sheets of paper without using a ruler. (2 marks)

38. A stadium seats 9,000 people. During a match 6,450 seats are taken. How many seats are empty? (3 marks)

39. Work out 6,003 − 2,475 and check your answer by adding. (4 marks)

40. Change 150 minutes to hours and minutes, and change 35 days to weeks. (3 marks)

41. Describe how to make a 1/2 L mark on an unmarked bottle using a 1 L container. (3 marks)

42. Describe how the length of a shadow changes from morning to afternoon and explain how this can help us to estimate the time of day. (4 marks)

43. Draw a rectangle 6 cm long and 3 cm wide and label its sides. (3 marks)

44. Write 0.8 and 0.37 as fractions. (2 marks)

45. Round 47, 342 and 995 to the nearest ten. (3 marks)

46. List three properties of a square. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 9
   The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. There are 9 of them.

2. C — 6
   The factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. There are 6 of them.

3. C — 380
   Look at the ones digit 9. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 379 rounds to 380.

4. C — 830
   Look at the ones digit 1. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 831 rounds to 830.

5. D — 4,212 pupils
   Add 1,845 + 2,367 = 4,212 pupils.

6. A — Difference
   Difference means how much bigger one number is than the other, so we subtract.

7. D — 864
   36 × 4 = 144 and 36 × 20 = 720. 144 + 720 = 864.

8. A — 48
   The rule is multiply by 2. 24 × 2 = 48.

9. A — 1,560
   52 × 3 = 156, then × 10 gives 1,560.

10. D — 7
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 700 ÷ 100 = 7.

11. D — 23
   4 × 23 = 92, so 92 ÷ 4 = 23.

12. C — 13
   7 × 13 = 91, so 91 ÷ 7 = 13.

13. D — 3 2/5
   17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 2/5, so 17/5 = 3 2/5.

14. C — 1.2
   Compare the tenths first. 1.2 is greater than 1.19.

15. B — k − 6
   The key words tell us the operation. "6 less than k" is written k − 6.

16. B — 4 × m
   A number written next to a letter means multiply. 4m is 4 times m.

17. D — 8 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 11 − 3 = 8 cm.

18. C — 4 m
   400 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 0. So 400 cm = 4 m.

19. C — 100 square units
   Area = 10 × 10 = 100 square units.

20. D — 25 square units
   Area = 5 × 5 = 25 square units.

21. B — 5
   Layers = 100 ÷ 20 = 5.

22. D — 30 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 2 = 10 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 10 × 3 = 30 blocks.

23. B — 64 blocks
   One layer has 4 × 4 = 16 blocks. There are 4 layers, so the volume is 16 × 4 = 64 blocks.

24. B — 3 1/2 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 2 L + 1 1/2 L = 3 1/2 L.

25. B — 4
   Four quarters make one whole kilogram.

26. B — 60 minutes
   The minute hand takes one hour, which is 60 minutes.

27. A — 5 weeks
   35 ÷ 7 = 5 remainder 0, so 35 days = 5 weeks.

28. D — Amount paid − total cost
   Change is what remains of the money paid after taking away the cost.

29. B — A flat shape
   A plane figure is a flat shape with length and width but no thickness.

30. B — 10
   Add all the numbers: 6 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 64 blocks
   Working / marking points: 4 × 4 = 16 per layer (1 mark); 16 × 4 (1 mark); 64 blocks (1 mark).

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) 6:30 a.m. (b) 3:15 p.m. (c) 7:30 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct time with a.m. or p.m.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6,325 eggs
   Working / marking points: Ones 0 + 5 = 5; tens 5 + 7 = 12 write 2 carry 1; hundreds 4 + 8 + 1 = 13 write 3 carry 1; thousands 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. 1 mark for method, 1 for regrouping, 1 for answer with unit.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Proper: 3/8 and 7/10. Improper: 11/5 and 9/9. Mixed: 2 1/2.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group and 1 mark for placing all five correctly.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: d − 45. When d = 100, she has 100 − 45 = 55 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for d − 45, 1 mark for the substitution, 1 mark for 55 shillings.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: 150 tiles; 144 tiles unbroken
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 15 × 10, 1 mark for 150, 1 mark for 150 − 6, 1 mark for 144.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put one sheet on top of the other with their corners lined up. The sheet that sticks out has the bigger area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for placing one on the other and 1 mark for saying the one that sticks out is bigger.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,550 seats
   Working / marking points: 9,000 − 6,450 with regrouping across zeros. 1 mark for the setup, 1 mark for regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3,528. Check: 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct regrouping across the zeros, 1 mark for the answer, 1 mark for the check.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. 35 days = 5 weeks.
   Working / marking points: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30 (1 mark for 2 h 30 min); 35 ÷ 7 = 5 (1 mark for 5 weeks); 1 mark for division working.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 1 L of water into one bottle. Share it into two identical bottles until the levels match. Mark the water level on one bottle as 1/2 L.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for starting with 1 L, 1 mark for sharing into two equal levels, 1 mark for marking 1/2 L.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: In the morning shadows are long, they get shorter towards midday when they are very short, and then get longer again in the afternoon. A very short shadow means it is about midday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for long in the morning, 1 mark for short at midday, 1 mark for long again in the afternoon, 1 mark for estimating time.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle with two sides 6 cm and two sides 3 cm and square corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four straight sides with square corners, 1 mark for correct lengths, 1 mark for labels.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8/10 and 37/100
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fraction.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 50, 340 and 1,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rounding. 995 goes up to 1,000 because the ones digit is 5.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Four equal sides, four right angles and four lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct property.
